title: The role of deliberate practice in the acquisition of expert performance.
population: Violinists and pianists at a Berlin academy
finding: Best violinists had accumulated about 10,000 solitary practice hours by age 20, roughly double the least accomplished group.

title: Deliberate Practice and Acquisition of Expert Performance: A General Overview
finding: Expert performance follows from goal-directed practice with feedback at the edge of current ability.

title: Long-term working memory.
population: Experts in memory, chess, medicine, reading
finding: Experts use retrieval structures in long-term memory to extend working memory within their domain.

title: Deliberate Practice and Performance in Music, Games, Sports, Education, and Professions: A Meta-Analysis
finding: Deliberate practice explains a modest share of performance variance, largest in predictable domains.

effect.value: Variance explained: games 26%, music 21%, sports 18%, education 4%, professions <1%

title: The Relationship Between Deliberate Practice and Performance in Sports
finding: Practice explains 18% of sports performance variance and 1% among elite athletes.

title: The deliberate practice view: An evaluation of definitions, claims, and empirical evidence
finding: Replication found best violinists did not practice more than good violinists; practice explained about a quarter of variance.

title: Deliberate practice: Is that all it takes to become an expert?
finding: Deliberate practice explains about a third of variance in chess and music; most variance lies elsewhere.

title: Summing up hours of any type of practice versus identifying optimal practice activities: commentary on Macnamara, Moreau, and Hambrick
finding: Argues the meta-analysis pooled practice types that do not meet the deliberate practice definition.

title: Expert memory: a comparison of four theories
finding: Template theory beats rival accounts of expert recall.

title: Perception in chess
finding: Masters recall legal positions far better than novices; the advantage vanishes for random positions.

title: Templates in Chess Memory: A Mechanism for Recalling Several Boards
finding: Experts recall several boards at once via retrieval templates.

title: Chunking mechanisms in human learning
finding: Chunking explains expert perception and learning rates across domains.

title: Practice and starting age in chess: individual differences in the paths to expertise
finding: Masters vary widely in hours to master level (about 3,000 to 23,000); early start predicts higher rating.

title: The role of practice in chess: A longitudinal study
finding: Practice is necessary but large individual differences remain.

title: Do the benefits of chess instruction transfer to academic and cognitive skills? A meta-analysis
population: 24 studies of chess training in children
finding: Chess shows small transfer that disappears in well-controlled studies.

effect.value: d = 0.34 overall; near zero with active controls

title: Does Far Transfer Exist? Negative Evidence From Chess, Music, and Working Memory Training
finding: Far transfer from cognitive training is near zero once design quality is controlled.

title: Working Memory Training in Typically Developing Children: A Multilevel Meta-Analysis
finding: Near transfer exists; far transfer is null after correcting for publication bias and placebo.

title: Near and Far Transfer in Cognitive Training: A Second-Order Meta-Analysis
finding: Far transfer across training types is close to zero.

title: Cognitive and academic benefits of music training with children: A multilevel meta-analysis
finding: Music training shows no reliable far transfer in randomized, actively controlled studies.

title: When and where do we apply what we learn? A taxonomy for far transfer
finding: Proposes nine dimensions of transfer distance (knowledge domain, context, time, modality).

title: Schema induction and analogical transfer
finding: Comparing two analogues induces a schema that transfers; one analogue rarely does.

title: Learning and transfer: A general role for analogical encoding.
finding: Comparing cases during learning triples later transfer.

title: Learning Through Case Comparisons: A Meta-Analytic Review
finding: Case comparison improves learning.

title: Transfer of learning
finding: Distinguishes low-road and high-road transfer.

title: The influence of improvement in one mental function upon the efficiency of other functions. (I).
finding: Training one mental function barely improves others; identical elements drive transfer.

title: The transfer of cognitive skill
finding: Transfer is predicted by shared production rules.

title: Range: Why generalists triumph in a specialized world
finding: Argues breadth and late specialization pay off in wicked domains.

title: International medallists’ and non-medallists’ developmental sport activities – a matched-pairs analysis
finding: Medallists did more other-sport practice in youth and started main-sport specialization later.

title: What Makes a Champion? Early Multidisciplinary Practice, Not Early Specialization, Predicts World-Class Performance
finding: World-class adult athletes started main sport later, had less early main-sport practice and more multi-sport practice than national-class peers.

title: Multidisciplinary practice and world-class performance in science, music and chess
finding: Pattern of early breadth and later specialization appears in science and music too.

title: Elite youth soccer players' development pathways
finding: Junior success poorly predicts senior success.

title: Predictors of Junior Versus Senior Elite Performance are Opposite: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Participation Patterns
finding: Early specialization predicts junior success and is negatively linked to senior success.

title: Creativity in the knowledge economy: Specialists, generalists, and the effects of field dynamics
finding: Generalists outperform specialists in fast-changing fields; specialists win in stable ones.

title: Prominent but less productive: The impact of interdisciplinarity on scientists' research
finding: Interdisciplinary research raises visibility and lowers productivity.

title: Bias against Novelty in Science: A Cautionary Tale for Users of Bibliometric Indicators
finding: Novel papers take longer to be cited and become top cited more often over 15 years.

title: Atypical Combinations and Scientific Impact
finding: High-impact papers combine conventional references with a small injection of atypical combinations.

effect.value: Hit rate about double for papers with both

title: The Burden of Knowledge and the “Death of the Renaissance Man”: Is Innovation Getting Harder?
finding: Age at first invention rises and specialization narrows as knowledge accumulates.

effect.value: Age at first invention up ~0.6 years per decade

title: The Increasing Dominance of Teams in Production of Knowledge
finding: Teams now produce most high-impact work in all fields.

title: Large teams develop and small teams disrupt science and technology
finding: Small teams produce more disruptive work; large teams develop existing ideas.

title: Age and Great Invention
finding: Peak age of great achievement rose over the 20th century.

title: Creative productivity: A predictive and explanatory model of career trajectories and landmarks.
finding: Equal-odds rule: hits scale with total output.

title: Talent and its development: An emergenic and epigenetic model.
finding: Talent as multiplicative components that develop over time.

title: Varieties of (Scientific) Creativity: A Hierarchical Model of Domain-Specific Disposition, Development, and Achievement
finding: Hierarchy of the sciences shapes the traits and development paths of creators.

title: Tracking exceptional human capital over two decades
population: SMPY top 1 in 10,000 at age 13 and grad students
finding: Precocious reasoners reach top creative and occupational outcomes at high rates.

title: Creativity and Occupational Accomplishments Among Intellectually Precocious Youths: An Age 13 to Age 33 Longitudinal Study.
finding: Ability differences within the top 1% predict doctorates, patents and publications.

title: Contrasting Intellectual Patterns Predict Creativity in the Arts and Sciences
finding: Math-verbal tilt at 13 predicts the domain of later creative achievement.

title: Life Paths and Accomplishments of Mathematically Precocious Males and Females Four Decades Later
finding: Precocious youth earned doctorates, patents and senior positions at many times base rates.

title: Creativity and technical innovation: spatial ability's unique role
finding: Spatial ability at 13 adds prediction of patents and publications beyond math and verbal.

title: Psychological Constellations Assessed at Age 13 Predict Distinct Forms of Eminence 35 Years Later
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 AERA Annual Meeting
finding: Ability and interest profiles at 13 predict different kinds of eminence.

title: Arts Foster Scientific Success: Avocations of Nobel, National Academy, Royal Society, and Sigma Xi Members
venue: Journal of Psychology of Science and Technology
finding: Nobel laureates are about three times more likely than average scientists to have an arts or crafts avocation.

title: Multiple Giftedness in Adults: The Case of Polymaths
finding: Polymathy is common among eminent creators; skills transfer through shared thinking tools.

title: Correlations Between Avocations, Scientific Style, Work Habits, and Professional Impact of Scientists
finding: Scientists with more avocations had higher impact.

title: Polymathy: A New Outlook
finding: Defines polymathy through breadth, depth and integration across domains.

title: POLYMATHIC LEADERSHIP: THEORETICAL FOUNDATION AND CONSTRUCT DEVELOPMENT
finding: Proposes polymathic leadership construct.

title: The polymath: A cultural history from Leonardo da Vinci to Susan Sontag
finding: Polymaths flourished when knowledge was smaller; specialization has made them rarer.

title: The Amusement Park Theory of creativity
finding: Creativity has general and domain-specific layers.

title: The Case for Domain Specificity of Creativity
finding: Creative performance correlates weakly across domains.

title: Babel no more: The search for the world's most extraordinary language learners
finding: Hyperpolyglots cluster at around 11 languages actively used and report heavy daily input and practice.

title: Advanced proficiency and exceptional ability in second languages
finding: Exceptional learners combine aptitude, motivation and many hours; aptitude matters most for late learners.

title: Hudson on hyperpolyglots
finding: Proposes six or more languages as a working threshold.

title: Age of onset, length of residence, language aptitude, and ultimate L2 attainment in three linguistic domains
finding: Late learners who pass as native have high aptitude.

title: Age of Onset and Nativelikeness in a Second Language: Listener Perception Versus Linguistic Scrutiny
finding: Under close scrutiny almost no late learner is fully nativelike.

title: A critical period for second language acquisition: Evidence from 2/3 million English speakers
finding: Grammar learning ability stays high until about 17 and declines after.

title: THE CONSTRUCT VALIDITY OF LANGUAGE APTITUDE
finding: Aptitude correlates with L2 proficiency.

title: The additive effect of bilingualism on third language acquisition: A review
finding: Bilinguals tend to learn a third language faster.

title: L3 syntactic transfer selectivity and typological determinacy: The typological primacy model
finding: L3 transfer draws on the language perceived as structurally closest.

title: Crosslinguistic influence in the acquisition of a third language: The Linguistic Proximity Model
finding: Transfer occurs property by property from both prior languages.

title: Linguistic Distance: A Quantitative Measure of the Distance between English and Other Languages
population: US-trained English speakers learning other languages
finding: Difficulty scores quantify linguistic distance from English.

title: Cross-language distance influences receptive vocabulary outcomes of immigrants
finding: Distance between L1 and Dutch predicts proficiency.

title: Cross-linguistic Similarity in Foreign Language Learning
population: Finnish and Swedish speakers learning English
finding: Perceived similarity drives positive transfer early on.

title: A Dynamic Systems Theory approach to second language acquisition
finding: Languages in one mind interact; attrition and growth compete for resources.

title: Semantic memory content in permastore: Fifty years of memory for Spanish learned in school.
population: 773 people, 1 to 50 years after Spanish courses
finding: Retention drops over 3 to 6 years, then stabilizes for decades in permastore.

title: Maintenance of Foreign Language Vocabulary and the Spacing Effect
finding: Wider spacing between relearning sessions gave better retention 5 years later.

title: Lifetime maintenance of high school mathematics content.
finding: Algebra retention for 50 years depended on taking courses beyond the content.

title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis.
finding: Spacing raises long-term retention; optimal gap grows with retention interval.

title: Spacing effects in learning: A temporal ridgeline of optimal retention
finding: Optimal gap is about 10 to 20% of the retention interval.

title: Replication and Analysis of Ebbinghaus’ Forgetting Curve
finding: Forgetting curve replicated.

title: Test-enhanced learning: Taking memory tests improves long-term retention
finding: Retrieval practice beats restudy at one week.

title: The effect of testing versus restudy on retention: A meta-analytic review of the testing effect.
finding: Testing beats restudy.

title: Rethinking the Use of Tests: A Meta-Analysis of Practice Testing
finding: Practice tests improve learning.

title: Improving Students’ Learning With Effective Learning Techniques
venue: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
finding: Practice testing and distributed practice rated high utility.

title: Abstracting Concepts and Patterns: Is Spacing the "Enemy of Induction"?
finding: Interleaved study improved induction though learners judged blocking better.

title: The shuffling of mathematics problems improves learning
finding: Interleaved math practice tripled test scores a week later.

title: Is interleaved practice superior to blocked practice? A meta-analysis
finding: Interleaving helps when categories are similar, not with words or dissimilar items.

effect.value: g = 0.42 overall; 0.67 paintings; negative for words

title: A randomized controlled trial of interleaved mathematics practice.
finding: Interleaved practice raised test scores a month later.

title: Contextual interference effects on the acquisition, retention, and transfer of a motor skill.
venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Learning and Memory
finding: Random practice slowed acquisition and improved retention and transfer.

title: Remembering can cause forgetting: Retrieval dynamics in long-term memory
finding: Retrieving some items suppresses related items.

title: Inhibiting your native language: The role of retrieval-induced forgetting during second-language acquisition
finding: Speaking a new language suppresses native-language word access.

title: Interference and forgetting.
finding: Proactive interference from prior lists drives most forgetting.

title: A new theory of disuse and an old theory of stimulus fluctuation
finding: Storage and retrieval strength separate; relearning after forgetting yields larger gains.

title: Language attrition
finding: Attrition depends on age, use and proficiency; high proficiency resists loss.

title: Language attrition: Disuse and its effects
finding: Disuse time predicts loss only after proficiency and contact controls.

title: The Attrition of Foreign-Language Skills: A Literature Review
finding: Receptive skills resist loss; productive skills decline first.

title: Insights into the ageing mind: a view from cognitive neuroscience
finding: Processing speed and episodic memory decline; knowledge holds.

title: When does age-related cognitive decline begin?
finding: Several abilities begin declining in the late 20s and early 30s.

title: When Does Cognitive Functioning Peak? The Asynchronous Rise and Fall of Different Cognitive Abilities Across the Life Span
finding: Abilities peak at different ages; vocabulary peaks after 60.

title: The Impact of Sustained Engagement on Cognitive Function in Older Adults
finding: Learning demanding new skills (quilting, photography) improved episodic memory.

title: Does bilingualism influence cognitive aging?
finding: Bilinguals showed better cognition at 70 than predicted from age-11 scores.

title: Bilingual advantages in executive functioning either do not exist or are restricted to very specific and undetermined circumstances
finding: The bilingual executive advantage is absent in large samples.

title: Is bilingualism associated with enhanced executive functioning in adults? A meta-analytic review.
finding: No reliable bilingual advantage after correcting for publication bias.

title: Bilingualism: consequences for mind and brain
finding: Argues bilingualism supports executive control and delays dementia.

title: Is it ever too late to learn a language? A randomized controlled trial on cognitive benefits of language learning in older adults
finding: Language learning showed no cognitive gains beyond an active control.

title: Generative AI Can Harm Learning
finding: GPT-4 base tutor raised practice scores 48% and lowered exam scores 17%; guarded tutor erased the harm.

title: AI Tutoring Outperforms Active Learning
venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
finding: AI tutor doubled learning gains versus in-class active learning in less time.

effect.value: Learning gains about 2x; effect 0.73 to 1.3 SD

title: Tutor CoPilot: A Human-AI Approach for Scaling Real-Time Expertise
venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
finding: LLM guidance for tutors raised topic mastery 4 points, 9 points for weaker tutors.

effect.value: +4 pp mastery; +9 pp for lowest-rated tutors

title: From Chalkboards to Chatbots: Evaluating the Impact of Generative AI on Learning Outcomes in Nigeria
finding: After-school GPT-4 tutoring improved English scores.

title: The Relative Effectiveness of Human Tutoring, Intelligent Tutoring Systems, and Other Tutoring Systems
finding: Step-based ITS nearly match human tutoring.

title: Effectiveness of Intelligent Tutoring Systems
finding: ITS raise test scores.

title: The 2 Sigma Problem: The Search for Methods of Group Instruction as Effective as One-to-One Tutoring
finding: One-to-one mastery tutoring produced a 2 SD gain.

title: Interpreting Effect Sizes of Education Interventions
finding: Median education RCT effect is about 0.10 SD; 0.20 is large.

title: AI meets the classroom: When do large language models harm learning?
finding: LLM use helps when it complements practice and harms when it substitutes.

title: Beware of metacognitive laziness: Effects of generative artificial intelligence on learning motivation, processes, and performance
finding: ChatGPT raised essay scores and did not improve knowledge gain or transfer.

title: Your brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of cognitive debt when using an AI assistant for essay writing task
finding: LLM writers showed lower neural engagement and recall of their own essays.

title: A Trainable Spaced Repetition Model for Language Learning
venue: Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
finding: Half-life regression predicts recall and raised engagement.

title: Enhancing human learning via spaced repetition optimization
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Optimal review schedule derived from stochastic control.

title: Knowledge tracing: Modeling the acquisition of procedural knowledge
finding: Bayesian knowledge tracing estimates per-skill mastery.

title: Deep knowledge tracing
finding: RNN knowledge tracing beats BKT on prediction.

title: Spaces for the assessment of knowledge
finding: Knowledge space theory models prerequisite structure as feasible knowledge states.

title: The Assessment of Knowledge, in Theory and in Practice
finding: Knowledge space theory runs at scale in ALEKS.

title: Measuring Prerequisite Relations Among Concepts
venue: Proceedings of the 2015 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
finding: Reference distance infers prerequisite relations from links.

title: Prerequisite Relation Learning for Concepts in MOOCs
venue:
Proceedings of the 55th Annual Meeting of the Association for
          Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
finding: Features from course text predict concept prerequisites.

title: The acquisition of knowledge
finding: Learning hierarchies: mastering subordinate skills enables superordinate ones.

title: The theory underlying concept maps and how to construct and use them
finding: Concept maps make prerequisite structure explicit.

title: Learning With Concept and Knowledge Maps: A Meta-Analysis
finding: Concept mapping improves retention and transfer.

effect.value: d = 0.82 vs reading; smaller vs discussion

title: Why minimal guidance during instruction does not work
finding: Novices learn more from guided instruction than discovery.

title: The expertise reversal effect
finding: Methods that help novices hinder experts.

title: Cognitive Load During Problem Solving: Effects on Learning
finding: Means-ends search loads working memory and slows schema learning.

title: Categorization and Representation of Physics Problems by Experts and Novices*
finding: Experts sort by deep principles; novices by surface features.

title: A theory of adult intellectual development: Process, personality, interests, and knowledge
finding: Adult knowledge grows through investment of fluid ability guided by interests.

title: Domain-specific knowledge as the dark matter of adult intelligence
finding: Middle-aged adults know more across domains than young adults.

title: General Mental Ability in the World of Work: Occupational Attainment and Job Performance.
venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
finding: General mental ability predicts job performance and training success.

title: Revisiting meta-analytic estimates of validity in personnel selection
finding: Corrected validities lower than earlier estimates.

title: Top 10 Replicated Findings From Behavioral Genetics
finding: Abilities are heritable and heritability of intelligence rises with age.

title: Practice does not make perfect: No causal effect of music practice on music ability
finding: Within identical twin pairs, practice differences did not predict ability differences.

title: Rethinking expertise: A multifactorial gene–environment interaction model of expert performance.
finding: Expertise arises from genes, practice and their interaction.

title: Beyond born versus made: A new look at expertise
finding: Many factors beyond practice shape expertise, including working memory and starting age.

title: The impact of deliberate practice on the development of chess skill
finding: Serious solo study predicts rating growth.

title: The joint influence of intelligence and practice on skill development throughout the life span
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Ability and practice interact; higher ability gains more per game.

title: Longitudinal Effects of Different Types of Practice on the Development of Chess Expertise
finding: Games played and study both drive rating, with diminishing returns.

title: Mechanisms of skill acquisition and the law of practice
finding: Performance improves as a power function of practice.

title: The power law repealed: The case for an exponential law of practice
finding: Individual curves fit exponential better than power functions.

title: Acquisition of cognitive skill.
finding: ACT theory: declarative knowledge compiles into procedures.

title: Practice in a second language: Perspectives from applied linguistics and cognitive psychology
finding: Skill acquisition theory applies to L2: practice proceduralizes declarative rules.

title: Principles and Practice in Second Language Acquisition
finding: Comprehensible input is the driver of acquisition.

title: Communicative competence: Some roles of comprehensible input and comprehensible output in its development
finding: Immersion students understand well and speak less accurately; output pushes form.

title: How Large a Vocabulary is Needed For Reading and Listening?
finding: 8,000 to 9,000 word families give 98% coverage of written text.

title: Unknown vocabulary density and reading comprehension
finding: 98% known-word coverage needed for unassisted comprehension.

title: The effectiveness of ER on reading proficiency: A meta-analysis
finding: Extensive reading improves reading proficiency.

title: Effectiveness of L2 Instruction: A Research Synthesis and Quantitative Meta‐analysis
finding: Explicit L2 instruction beats implicit.

title: Effects of explicit and implicit instruction on L2 knowledge
finding: Explicit instruction yields larger and durable gains.

title: Foreign language training: language difficulty rankings
finding: Category I languages take 600 to 750 class hours, Category IV about 2,200 for English speakers.

title: Understanding expertise: A multi-disciplinary approach
finding: Synthesizes chunking, templates and practice evidence.

title: Studies of Expertise from Psychological Perspectives
venue: The Cambridge Handbook of Expertise and Expert Performance
finding: Expertise is domain-limited and rarely transfers.

title: Science of science
finding: Reviews team, career and impact regularities in science.

title: Fresh teams are associated with original and multidisciplinary research
population: Papers by fresh vs repeat teams
finding: Teams of new collaborators produce more original, multidisciplinary work.

title: Papers and patents are becoming less disruptive over time
finding: Disruptiveness declined across fields since 1945.

title: Hot streaks in artistic, cultural, and scientific careers
finding: Most careers have one hot streak at a random time.

title: Understanding the onset of hot streaks across artistic, cultural, and scientific careers
finding: Hot streaks follow periods of exploration then exploitation.

title: Quantifying the evolution of individual scientific impact
finding: The highest-impact paper falls at random within a career.

title: Increasing trend of scientists to switch between topics
finding: Scientists switch topics more often; switching carries an impact penalty.

title: Long-Distance Interdisciplinarity Leads to Higher Scientific Impact
finding: Citing distant disciplines associates with higher long-run impact.

finding: Risky innovative strategies earn more citations and are rarer.

finding: Experts in the method transfer reasoning to new content; content experts without method do not.

title: Analogical transfer, problem similarity, and expertise.
venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
finding: Experts retrieve analogies by structure; novices by surface.

title: Analysis of the brain of a hyperpolyglot
finding: Broca area of a 60-language polyglot showed distinct cytoarchitecture.

title: Reduced language network responses to native language in polyglots
finding: Polyglots show smaller language network responses to native language.

finding: Language learning tracks input frequency.

title: On the Form of Forgetting
population: adult recall and recognition, delays up to two weeks
finding: Forgetting curves fit a power function better than an exponential.

title: Reflections of the Environment in Memory
finding: The odds an item is needed fall as a power function of time since its last use, matching memory retention.
